author: Mark Thompson
title: Multiple Injuries Reported | Accident Updates
text:
Parachute Plane Crashes in New Jersey, Injuring Over 10 A plane dedicated to skydiving crashed Wednesday afternoon in Gloucester County, New Jersey, leaving more than 10 people injured, according to local authorities. The incident occurred near the Cross Keys airport in Williamstown around 5:30 pm local time, prompting a large emergency response.
According to reports from CNBC, the aircraft, a Cessna 208B, was carrying 15 people when it “diverted towards the end of the track at the airport,” as cited by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) in a statement to Nj.com. Five of the injured were quickly transported to nearby healthcare centers. The extent of their injuries ranges from minor to serious.
Gloucester County’s emergency management office reported a “multi-casualty incident” involving a downed plane at the Cross Keys airport via a Facebook post, urging the public to avoid the area to allow emergency personnel access.
The cause of the crash remains unknown at this time, and an investigation is underway. Authorities have not yet released details regarding the circumstances that led to the plane leaving the runway.
This is a developing story. Further updates will be provided as they become available.
